name: Balanced Dollar
oneLiner: bnUSD is Balanced's decentralized dollar stablecoin on ICON, minted from overcollateralized CDPs against sICX and bridged cross-chain via xCall.
collateral: Overcollateralized loans on ICON against sICX (staked ICX), with cross-chain Hub collateral support for assets bridged in via Balanced's xCall infrastructure

Additional active deployments on Archway and Havah (also not Pharos-supported), and on Optimism, are visible in DefiLlama but excluded from contracts[] until those chains are wired into Pharos.

launchPhaseDetail: Pilot phase following successful September 2025 proof of concept; not yet in public circulation. BDACS is South Korea's regulated digital-asset custodian; Woori Bank holds the won reserves and participated directly in the PoC. Initial deployment on Avalanche (cited by KISA for reliability in public-sector use); KRW1 expanded to Polygon in December 2025 for broader payments, remittances, and enterprise reach. October 2025 MoU with Circle positions KRW1 for deployment on Arc (Circle's new Layer 1), where it joins national stablecoin issuers from Japan, Brazil, Mexico, and the Philippines. February 2026 Plume partnership positions KRW1 as Korean institutional settlement rail for tokenized RWA. May 2026 Aptos Foundation partnership brings KRW1 to its first non-EVM chain, leveraging Aptos's payment infrastructure for cross-border remittances and RWA tokenisation. A February 2026 MoU with Com2uS Holdings targets KRW1-based payment infrastructure on the XPLA/CONX chain. Korea's Digital Asset Basic Act — the gate for commercial launch — was excluded from the National Assembly's pre-recess agenda on May 12 2026, with debate not expected to resume until a new parliamentary session after the June 3 elections, pushing any enactment into H2 2026 or later. Commercial launch contingent on that framework.

genius.notes: On December 12, 2025, the OCC granted Paxos Trust Company conditional approval to convert from its NYDFS limited purpose trust charter to a national trust bank charter (OCC NR-2025-125). This is a conditional trust-charter conversion, not a PPSI approval under the GENIUS Act (whose application framework remains in proposed-rules rulemaking). Paxos publicly announced PYUSD will align with GENIUS Act requirements as rules are finalized. The authorizationStatus remains issuer-announced-intent because no PPSI approval framework or application process yet exists. The OCC rulemaking (Bulletin 2026-3) is also scrutinizing PayPal's 4% PYUSD reward program as a potential indirect interest payment prohibited under GENIUS.

launchPhaseDetail: Companion to the already-tracked RGBP (Revolut GBP). Revolut secured a MiCA CASP licence from Cyprus (CySEC) on Oct 23 2025 and operates an existing EMI licence in Lithuania — the legal foundations for issuing e-money tokens under MiCA Title IV. In October 2025, Revolut launched fee-free 1:1 USD↔stablecoin swaps (USDC/USDT on Ethereum, Solana, and Tron) for its 65M users; stablecoin payment volumes on the platform surged 156% in 2025 to ~$10.5B. In February 2026, the FCA selected Revolut as one of 4 firms (from 20 applicants) for a UK stablecoin payment testing pilot — though that sandbox is specifically for a GBP token, not USD. Revolut received a full UK banking licence from the PRA (Mar 11 2026) and filed an OCC national bank charter application for Revolut Bank US, N.A. (Mar 5 2026, targeting a 2027 US launch with built-in stablecoin access). A Revolut-branded proprietary USD stablecoin has not been officially confirmed; the USD path runs through the Lithuanian EMI / MiCA EMT route, and Polymarket currently puts the probability at ~33% by year-end 2026. Specific ticker, chain selection, and reserve disclosure model remain unannounced.

applicabilityBasis.summary: sUSD is explicitly designed as a yield-bearing stablecoin that passes T-bill interest to holders via Solana Token-2022 interest extension. The GENIUS Act Section 4(a)(11) prohibits permitted payment stablecoin issuers from paying any form of interest or yield to holders solely in connection with holding the stablecoin. Whether sUSD qualifies as a 'payment stablecoin' subject to this prohibition (and therefore potentially non-compliant as currently structured) or falls outside the payment-stablecoin definition as a yield-bearing investment instrument remains unresolved pending final GENIUS Act implementing regulations. No official guidance has classified yield-bearing RWA-backed stablecoins. Applicability is genuinely unclear.

genius.notes: Solayer Labs, Inc. is a US-incorporated company headquartered in San Francisco (CA corp, doc #6557004). sUSD is a yield-bearing stablecoin backed by US Treasury bills via a partnership with OpenEden (Moody's-rated RWA platform). The yield is passed to holders through Solana Token-2022 interest extension mechanics — a design that sits in regulatory tension with the GENIUS Act's yield prohibition on payment stablecoin issuers. No GENIUS authorization, application, or registration found. No enforcement action found. The applicability question (payment stablecoin vs. excluded yield instrument) will only be resolved once final GENIUS implementing regulations are issued.

genius.notes: Anchorage Digital Bank is an uninsured OCC-chartered national trust bank (the first federally chartered crypto bank, chartered January 2021). applicabilityBasis.summary: USDN is a rebasing yield-bearing stablecoin that accrues T-bill yield directly to holder balances every 30 seconds via M0's rebase mechanism. The Act also explicitly prohibits payment stablecoin issuers from paying any yield to holders — USDN's entire design is yield distribution. These structural features place USDN outside the GENIUS payment stablecoin definition.

genius.notes: USDN is a rebasing yield-bearing T-bill wrapper built on M0 infrastructure; it falls outside the GENIUS Act payment stablecoin definition because (1) it does not redeem at a fixed monetary value (balances rebase upward as yield accrues), and (2) its core design distributes yield directly to holders, which the Act prohibits for in-scope payment stablecoins. Noble's legal entity is NASD Inc (US-based); M0 provides infrastructure but is not the issuer. Noble announced migration from Cosmos appchain to EVM L1 in January 2026; USDN remains the flagship asset on the new chain.

obituary.epitaph: When one key minted eighty million
obituary.obituary: On 22 March 2026, an attacker exploited Resolv's single-EOA minter — no oracle, no amount cap, no max-mint guard — depositing 100K USDC and receiving 50M USR in return, then iterating until 80M unbacked USR existed for ~$25M of extracted ETH. USR crashed to $0.025 in 17 minutes; the RLP insurance layer absorbed the bad debt and was wiped out, dragging Stream Finance's $17M position down with it. Resolv burned 46M of the unbacked supply via a blacklist freeze, but USR never recovered — by April it traded at $0.16 with $95M of collateral against $173M of liabilities. Delta-neutral collateral and Apostro-attested reserves were no defense against an operator-level privilege failure.

name: WEMIX Dollar
oneLiner: WEMIX Dollar is the WEMIX ecosystem's centralized dollar token, backed by USDC and fiat reserve assets on the non-EVM-indexed WEMIX chain.
collateral: USDC and fiat reserve assets held for WEMIX Dollar on WEMIX3.0; issuer materials describe full collateralization by secure on-chain and off-chain assets.
pegMechanism: Issuer-managed mint and redemption system using WEMIX$ treasury collateral, DIOS stabilization, and USDC/fiat reserve management to keep WEMIX$ near one U.S. dollar.

applicabilityBasis.summary: WEMIX Dollar (WEMIX$) is a USD-pegged, fiat-backed stablecoin issued by WEMIX PTE. LTD. (Singapore) under a permissioned mint-and-redemption model collateralized by USDC and fiat reserves. It circulated as the native settlement currency of the WEMIX3.0 gaming blockchain and was accessible to US-person users via international exchanges, matching the GENIUS Act definition of a payment stablecoin. The issuer announced a wind-down and transition to USDC.e in 2025; circulating supply has declined significantly but remains non-zero as of mid-2026 (CoinGecko reports approximately 14.5M WEMIX$ in circulation). Applicability is assessed on the basis of the token's design and issuance during its active life.

genius.notes: WEMIX PTE. LTD. (UEN 201903432D, formerly WEMADE TREE PTE. LTD.) is a Singapore-incorporated subsidiary of South Korean game developer WEMADE. The issuer announced in 2025 that WEMIX$ would be wound down and replaced by USDC.e (Circle bridged USDC via Chainlink CCIP). As of June 2026, CoinGecko (the coin's configured detailProvider) reports approximately 14.5M WEMIX$ still in circulation with minimal trading activity (~$33/day volume on WEMIX.Fi), indicating the wind-down is substantially advanced but not yet complete. No GENIUS Act PPSI application, foreign-issuer registration, or authorization announcement has been located. The foreign exception status is not-applicable because the GENIUS Act's foreign-issuer registration framework (Treasury comparability rule) remains in proposed-rules phase as of June 2026 and no determinations have been made. The issuer has made no public announcement of intent to engage with the GENIUS framework.

applicabilityBasis.summary: YLDS is a face-amount certificate issued by Figure Certificate Company, registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (File No. 811-23913) and the Securities Act of 1933 (File No. 333-275154, effective February 18, 2025). The GENIUS Act (enacted as Public Law 119-27) expressly excludes from the definition of 'payment stablecoin' any digital asset that is a 'security' under the Investment Company Act. Face-amount certificates are a defined category of investment company security under that Act. YLDS therefore falls outside the GENIUS Act's jurisdiction and is exempt from its yield prohibition and PPSI requirements.

The issuer (Figure Certificate Company, CIK 0001974395) confirms YLDS is 'exempt from the yield prohibition in the GENIUS Act.' No GENIUS authorization, pathway, or enforcement assessment applies.
